<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Laugh Tough" /></noinclude><section begin="par106" />19:27, &c.; 29:10 ''now when Jacob had seen Rachel'' ({{GHGheb|text=בַּֽאֲשֶׁר רָאָה}})..., ''Jacob went near'', &c.; so also in clauses which express the completion or incompleteness of one action, &c., on the occurrence of another, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, &c.; cf. {{GHGpar|164|b}}, with the note, and c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|106|g}}
'''2.''' To represent actions, events, or states, which, although completed in the past, nevertheless extend their influence into the present (in English generally rendered by the present):

(''a'') Expressing facts which were accomplished long before, or conditions and attributes which were acquired long before, but of which the effects still remain in the present (present perfect), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=10|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הִסְתִּיר פָּנָיו|translate=he hath hidden his face}} (''and still keeps it hidden''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=143|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=פֵּרַ֫שְׂתִּי|translate=I have spread forth my hands}} (''and still keep them spread forth''). This applies particularly to a large number of perfects (almost exclusively of intransitive<ref>With regard to the great but very natural preponderance of intransitive verbs (expressing an existing state), cf. the lists in Knudtzon (see above, p. 309, note 2), pp. 117 and 122 in the Danish text.</ref> verbs, denoting affections or states of the mind) which in English can be rendered only by the present, or, in the case mentioned above under ''f'', by the imperfect.<ref>Cf. ''novi, odi, memini''; οἶδα, μέμνημαι, ἔοικα, δέδορκα, κέκραγα; in the New Testament, ἤλπικα, ἡγαπηκα.</ref> Thus, {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫עְתִּי|translate=I know}} (prop. ''I have perceived, have experienced'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יָדַ֫עְתִּי|translate=I know not}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=9}}, &c.; on the other hand, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=34}}, the context requires ''I knew not''; {{GHGheb|text=זָכַ֫רְנוּ|translate=we remember}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאֲנָה|translate=she refuseth}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָלַץ|translate=it exulteth}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׂמַ֫חְתִּי|translate=I rejoice}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּקֵּשׁ|translate=he requireth}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=12}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִוִּ֫יתִי|translate=I wait}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=130|verse=5}} (parallel with {{GHGheb|text=הוֹחָֽ֫לְתִּי}}); {{GHGheb|text=חָפַ֫צְתִּי|translate=I delight}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=9}} (mostly negative, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=11}}, &c.); {{GHGheb|text=אָהַ֫בְתִּי|translate=I love}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׂנֵ֫אתִי|translate=I hate}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָאַ֫סְתִּי|translate=I despise}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽעֲב֫וּנִי|translate=they abhor me}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּטַ֫חְתִּי|translate=I trust}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=25|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=חָסִ֫יתִי|translate=I put my trust}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=צָדַ֫קְתִּי|translate=I am righteous}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=פָּקַ֫דְתִּי|translate=I have decided to requite}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=2}}.—We may further include a number of verbs which express bodily characteristics or states, such as {{GHGheb|text=גָּדַ֫לְתָּ|translate=thou art great}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹ֫נְתִּי|translate=I am little}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּֽבְהוּ|translate=they are high}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=רָֽחֲקוּ|translate=they stand aloof}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=טֹ֫בוּ|translate=they are goodly}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָאווּ|translate=they are beautiful}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=זָקַ֫נְתִּי|translate=I am old}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָגַ֫עְתִּי|translate=I am weary}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=6|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׂבַ֫עְתִּי|translate=I am full}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=11}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|106|h}}
Rem. To the same category probably belong also the perfects after {{GHGheb|text=עַד־מָתַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=3}} ''how long hast thou'' already ''been refusing'' (and refusest still...? which really amounts to ''how long wilt thou refuse''?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=22}} (co-ordinate with the imperf.), and after {{GHGheb|text=עַד־אָ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|106|i}}
